findings.evidence: At c5ba7cc, qa-gate.sh:5642 invokes reconcile_tracker, but that function does not invariably write changed-files.txt. It unconditionally truncates reconcile-subtracted.txt at :1273, can return without touching changed-files.txt for a clean tree at :1385-1387, no survivors at :1522-1524, or an already-complete tracker at :1601-1603, and appends changed-files.txt only when to_add is non-empty at :1615-1625. The same cmd_approve body later exits 2 at :6990 before the durable approval write at :7784.
findings.description: The corrected safety conclusion is right, but the new qualifier again overstates the earlier write: reconcile_tracker has already run and may append changed-files.txt; it does not always do so. Say that it already writes/truncates reconciliation bookkeeping, or that it can append changed-files.txt.

findings.evidence: The value 13139e50... is exactly the content SHA-256 of git diff 91bfcc8^ 91bfcc8 -- CHANGELOG.md, as the envelope discloses. But .claude/agents/qa.md:398 and :420 define reviewed_hash as the request's change_set_hash; .claude/scripts/codex-review.sh:179-190 and :539 force that value; and docs/HOOKS.md:1748-1755 says REVIEW-ARTIFACT reviewed_hash shares the canonical changed-path-list hash with approval and rubric records. The envelope cannot alter that machine-field contract.
findings.description: This is an honest disclosure of what was hashed, but it is still a misuse of reviewed_hash in a REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 object. Preserve the diff digest in a separately named provenance field or explicitly nonconforming archival record; do not place it in the standardized change-set-binding field.
